name: Subset Teaching Dimension
definition: Let $\mathrm{STS}^{0}(h,\mathcal H)$ be the set of all ordinary minimum teaching samples for $h$. Given $k$ and a sample $S$, set $\mathrm{Cons}_{\mathrm{sub}}(S,\mathcal H,k)=\{h'\in\mathcal H:\exists S'\in\mathrm{STS}^{k}(h',\mathcal H), S\subseteq S'\}$. Then $\mathrm{STD}^{k+1}(h,\mathcal H)$ is the smallest $|S|$ for which this set is $\{h\}$, and $\mathrm{STS}^{k+1}(h,\mathcal H)$ contains all minimizers. Once these sets stabilize, the **Subset Teaching Dimension** is the maximum stabilized value over $h$.
graph_summary: Iterated cooperative teaching: a sample identifies a target by being contained in one of its previous minimum teaching samples and in no other target’s.
description: An iteratively defined, complement-symmetric teaching parameter. It is at most ordinary teaching dimension, but is neither comparable with Balbach nor recursive teaching dimension, and is neither subclass-, projection- nor conditioning-monotonic. Even strict increase at equal-valued coordinate branches fails.

monotonic.proof: Theorem 21 constructs, for every $u>2$, a class $\mathcal C$ with a subclass $\mathcal C'$ such that $\mathrm{STD}(\mathcal C)=2$ and $\mathrm{STD}(\mathcal C')=u$.

symmetric.proof: Complementing every concept exchanges positive and negative labels bijectively. This preserves ordinary minimum teaching samples, inclusion between samples, and hence every stage of the subset-teaching recursion.

p_monotonic.proof: The five-concept class {000,001,010,011,100} has STD one, but deleting the first coordinate gives the full two-cube, of STD two. The survey computes all minimum teaching samples at every iteration.

c_monotonic.proof: For the class {000,001,010,011,100}, STD is one, whereas conditioning the first coordinate to zero leaves the full two-cube, of STD two. All three original coordinates are active. See the complete iteration table in the survey.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: The same five-concept class has STD one. Its two branches at the second coordinate also have STD one: they are {00,01,10} and {00,01}. Thus even the strict-increase requirement at equal nonempty branches fails.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: The equal-branch plus-one identity fails on the same class: the whole class and both branches at the second coordinate all have STD one. This does not rely on imposing equality with the maximum at unequal branches.

doubly_monotonic.proof: Doubly monotonicity requires subfamily monotonicity, which Theorem 21 refutes.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires doubly monotonicity, which fails.
